# `silk/trace/perfetto`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Perfetto trace encoding for recorder batches and counter samples.

A Perfetto trace is a sequence of `TracePacket` messages, each one written as field 1 of the
`Trace` message. Bytes made of whole packets are a trace on their own, and so is a file that
several writers append whole packets to. The Perfetto UI and `trace_processor` open it, with each
span as a slice on the track of the thread that opened it, each log as an instant on the
process's `log` track, and each metric series and counter sample as a counter track.

Import as `Perfetto` with `import silk.trace.perfetto { Perfetto }`.

Public declarations: 2.

<a id="Perfetto"></a>

## `Perfetto`

```silk
pub struct Perfetto
```

One process's Perfetto packet sequence: the names it has interned and the tracks it has
described.

### When to use
Keep one `Perfetto` for each process that writes a trace, and pass it every batch and sample
the process writes, so that each name and track is written once. As a [`Sink`](./trace-sink.md#Sink) it writes each
batch to the active `Writer`.

### Details
The process ID numbers the sequence, so the packets of processes that append to one file at
the same time keep their interned names apart. A span becomes a slice on the track of the
thread that opened it, or on the process's `spans` track when the target gives no thread ID,
with its attributes, source location and error as arguments. A log becomes an instant named
by its template on the process's `log` track, with its message and severity. Each metric series
becomes a counter track named by its instrument and attributes; a histogram has no single value
over time and is left out. Times are the recorder's Unix nanoseconds.

### Gotchas
A trace viewer nests slices by their times. Two spans of one thread that start at the same
nanosecond nest in the order they were written, which is the order they ended, so a span and
its first child must start at different times. The recorder's tick counters ensure it on Apple
and Linux targets, where opening a span takes longer than one tick.

<a id="Perfetto.impl.encodeInto"></a>

### Method `encodeInto`

```silk
pub effect fn encodeInto(self: &mut Self, identity: &Resource, batch: &Batch<'_>, output: &mut Bytes) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Replaces the contents of `output` with the packets of `batch`, preceded by the descriptions
of the tracks and names they use first. `identity` names the process the first time.

<a id="Perfetto.impl.sample"></a>

### Method `sample`

```silk
pub effect fn sample(self: &mut Self, identity: &Resource, name: string<'static>, unit: CounterUnit, time: u64,
    value: f64, output: &mut Bytes) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends to `output` the value `value` of the counter `name` at `time`, in Unix nanoseconds,
and the counter's track the first time, measured in `unit`. `identity` names the process the
first time.
